title.narrative: GCERF Enhanced Resilience to Violent Extremism (Sahel & Littoral States)

description.narrative:
Fund replenishment, or core support with a soft geographic earmarking to the Sahel region, relevant West-African coastal states, and the Horn of Africa. GCERF’s Sahel programme is the point of departure, with the G5 Sahel countries and so-called ‘littoral states’ as the main beneficiaries. The Sahel programme focuses on the Liptako-Gourma region (“Fuseau Centre”) and is in the process to expanding it to other parts of the G5 countries: “Fuseau Ouest” (Mali-Mauritania border) and the “Fuseau Est” (Niger-Chad border). G5 Sahel consists of Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali, Mauritania and Niger. Ghana, Benin, Togo, Ivory Coast, and Nigeria fall into the category of so-called littoral states. The Norwegian grant will mainly be utilised in Mauritania, Chad, Ghana and Niger. Overall objective (impact): The emergence of resilient communities against violent extremism in the most vulnerable communities.
Target Groups: - Group 1: Internally and externally displaced young men and women living in host communities in rural areas. - Group 2: Bereaved households due to extremist, self-defence militias, or government forces operations. - Group 3: Local authority actors, including customary chiefs and religious leaders to enable existing structures to build sustainable pockets of peace.
All GCERF projects have a gender equality cross-cutting theme to ensure a conflict sensitive and inclusive response. In addition, each grantee benefits from tailored trainings for example on gender sensitive programming.
